requirements.controllingText: File-inspection status is the closed set INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF, which the application establishes; EXTERNAL_INSPECTION_CLAIMED, which is agent-asserted; INSPECTION_SUPPORTED, which is the claim plus complete consistent per-unit dispositions and source locations; and INSPECTION_ESTABLISHED_TO_REQUIRED_BASIS, which is the minimum basis the file's contract requires. Stage 01 completion requires INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF as an application fact and at least INSPECTION_SUPPORTED for every required file; the word inspected always means at the recorded basis and is never represented as an application-proven semantic fact. A required artifact whose semantic content is INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED and not proven immaterial leaves Stage 01 BLOCKED unless human authority removes it from project scope through a new input version.

requirements.controllingText: The unitization contract explicitly defines treatment of comments, annotations, tracked changes, metadata, embedded objects, inaccessible content, and unsupported formats. A supported subdivision cannot be replaced by one whole-file unit merely to make coverage vacuous. SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE_LIMITS/1 triggers a challenge when any one of these thresholds is exceeded: 1,048,576 stored bytes in one text or document artifact; 100 mechanically countable pages; 20 supplied files or archive members; 500 raw units; or 5,242,880 aggregate supplied bytes. A material uncovered unit, broad exclusion, INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED material, material uncertainty, contradiction, or operator request triggers regardless of size. These limits are centralized, versioned, and acceptance-tested and may be lowered but not raised without a new contract-profile identity.

SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE_LIMITS/1 triggers a challenge when any one of these thresholds is exceeded: 1,048,576 stored bytes in one text or document artifact; 100 mechanically countable pages; 20 supplied files or archive members; 500 raw units; or 5,242,880 aggregate supplied bytes. A material uncovered unit, broad exclusion, INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED material, material uncertainty, contradiction, or operator request triggers regardless of size. These limits are centralized, versioned, and acceptance-tested and may be lowered but not raised without a new contract-profile identity.

These limits are centralized, versioned, and acceptance-tested and may be lowered but not raised without a new contract-profile identity.

requirements.controllingText: The versioned source-class checklist derives from the closed generic class set — governing law and regulation; standards and specifications; controlling contracts and prior agreements; authoritative technical documentation; official registries and databases; scholarly and measurement literature; and project-supplied references — filtered by the Stage 01 objective and declared jurisdiction or system scope. Omitting an entire applicable class requires explicit reasoning and is challenged by the SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW. The contract also declares explicit stopping criteria: every registered location searched; query saturation, meaning no new candidate source in the final registered query round; authority-chain closure, meaning every authority cited by an accepted controlling source received a disposition; the declared date or version cutoff; a disposition for every inaccessible location; and the residual-risk statement. Search completion without every declared criterion is invalid.

requirements.controllingText: The external agent may ask concise human-authority questions in the external conversation. A human-origin answer first supplied there remains an EXTERNAL_CLAIM until the agent returns it in the response JSON and the application presents the exact extracted answer for one-action confirmation or correction. The resulting confirmation creates the HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION record and provenance link. Exact confirmation may be atomically co-accepted with the dependent proposal under Section 14.10; correction requires a replacement prompt. The operator is not required to retype the answer. Facts already present in current raw input or accepted human records are not reconfirmed.

The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. These commands write only their declared HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION fields and records, accept no agent-owned canonical fields, and accept no external response envelope.

The application never claims an uncaptured response was recorded.

Directory entries, timestamps, permissions, compression method, compression level, and path normalization are fixed by the registered archive profile. An archive mismatch does not alter the logical package identity; it rejects the transport representation.

It must use the registered deterministic archive profile and pass the archive safety rules. The current profile is closed-loop-archive-profile/1: a ZIP archive containing only STORE (uncompressed) entries, entries ordered by canonical-path unsigned byte order, the UTF-8 filename flag set, every timestamp fixed to 1980-01-01T00:00:00, no directory entries, no symlinks or special entries, no archive comment, no encryption, and no extra fields except a Zip64 field exactly where an entry or archive size requires it. The manifest is always at `manifest.json`; the authoritative prompt is at `instruction.txt`; an inbound response is at `response.json`. Directory entries, timestamps, permissions, compression method, compression level, and path normalization are fixed by the registered archive profile. An archive mismatch does not alter the logical package identity; it rejects the transport representation.

requirements.controllingText: The deterministic profile governs application-produced archives only. An inbound archive from an external actor is a nonauthoritative convenience container: it must pass the Section 19.9 safety rules, is exploded into named attachment slots with per-member byte verification, and its original bytes are preserved as evidence. External actors are never required to produce the deterministic profile; the authoritative inbound representation remains response.json plus attachment-slot files.

requirements.controllingText: Every artifact and package member is classified PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED, CREDENTIAL_SECRET, or UNKNOWN. CREDENTIAL_SECRET is never externally transferred. RESTRICTED or UNKNOWN content requires current recipient/provider suitability and human disclosure authorization. Package creation uses a derived allowlist, prohibited-member exclusion, known secret-pattern scan, path scan, disclosure check, and supported metadata inventory. A clean heuristic scan is not proof of absence. Redaction creates a new artifact and never silently replaces the original.

requirements.controllingText: Every artifact preserves rawFilename and has a safe displayFilename and canonicalPath under closed-loop-filename/1. Canonical comparison uses Unicode 15.1.0 NFC, case-sensitive identity, and separately checked Unicode 15.1.0 default-case-fold and registered platform-risk collision keys. Absolute paths, drive prefixes, NUL, control characters, empty segments, `.` and `..`, duplicate canonical paths, case-fold collisions, extraction-target collisions, and supported confusable collisions are rejected. An unauthorized rename never matches solely because bytes are equal.

atomicObligation.statement: The filename contract rejects absolute paths.

requirements.controllingText: Test IR is a topologically ordered directed acyclic graph. Every step has a unique application-validated stepId, one registered op, and an explicit inputs object. Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. requirements.controllingText: Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.

requirements.controllingText: When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

requirements.controllingText: EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

atomicObligation.statement: ANY_OF is accepted only when review establishes each branch alone suffices for the parent proposition.

requirements.controllingText: EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

It is either an authorized scope change creating new input and requirements versions, an authoritative waiver represented as a new governing obligation with its own proposition and evidence, or a blocker where authority is insufficient. Every exception records authority, reason, scope, effective period, affected propositions, independent challenge when obligations are reduced, and downstream invalidation.

requirements.controllingText: NFC normalization and default case folding use Unicode 15.1.0 data. Confusable detection uses the Unicode Technical Standard #39 confusables data published for Unicode 15.1.0. These exact data identities and table digests are recorded in the runtime registry and deployment manifest. A host Unicode implementation may be used only when startup and CI conformance fixtures establish the pinned results for every supported code-point class; otherwise the application uses bundled pinned tables. An unknown host/table mismatch blocks canonical filename normalization and package activation. Runtime upgrades do not silently change canonical identities; runtime or browser Unicode behavior may not silently redefine canonical identity. Every set-valued array has one named versioned normalizer. Every contentSha256, recordSha256, project hash, package hash, proof hash, scope hash, and terminal hash has a closed JSON-pointer inclusion and omission set registered in workflow-schema.js. No implementation selects preimage fields implicitly.

requirements.controllingText: For every registered hash kind, the preimage inclusion set is exactly the canonical fields of the subject record or manifest, excluding only the digest field itself and every field whose value depends on that digest, fields declared audit-only or derived-summary, and fields the owning schema explicitly excludes with a registered reason. The scope-hash preimage is exactly the Section 14.7 dimensions of the operation, and the terminal-hash preimage is exactly the records enumerated in Section 36.9. An unregistered hash kind or pointer set is UNDEFINED_HASH_PREIMAGE and blocks the computation and every dependent gate. Default array semantics are ordered and order-significant; an array is set-valued only when its JSON pointer is explicitly registered with an element-identity key, a duplicate rule that rejects duplicates, and a sort rule of canonical byte order over the element identity. An unregistered pointer treated as a set is UNDEFINED_SET_SEMANTICS and blocks.

requirements.controllingText: Reservation states are RESERVED, EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, RESPONSE_STAGED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, SUPERSEDED, or EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE. Only RESERVED, EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, and RESPONSE_STAGED can preserve package validity, and only when revision, scope, prompt, package, nonce, and target slot remain unchanged. EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, RESPONSE_STAGED, REJECTED, and CANCELLED are recorded as metadata-store operational events and do not increment canonical projectRevision. ACCEPTED commits the canonical project once. A later canonical scope change marks the reservation SUPERSEDED or EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE. No operational status event invalidates its own package.

atomicObligation.statement: ACCEPTED commits the canonical project once.

requirements.controllingText: Resuming an ORPHANED reservation verifies the same binding and changes no identity. A new authoritative reservation for the slot is prohibited until the old reservation is terminal. Its reservation reaches a terminal state, the same run target slot is re-reserved under Section 35.6, and the replacement attempt receives a new fresh context reserved for that run. The superseded context becomes historical, is excluded from the ten-distinct-context calculation, and its outputs cannot appear in any authorized input. Exactly the ten current accepted runs and their ten current distinct contexts satisfy Stage 11. An accepted run is never re-executed within the same iteration; a defect discovered in an accepted run routes through Stages 13-17.

A defect in the release-calculation semantics themselves is an implementation defect handled through the Sections 40-44 regression discipline, never by silently recalculating Stage 27.

requirements.controllingText: The application records a DELIVERY_ATTEMPT receipt containing the delivery ID, attempt ID, exact artifacts, byte hashes, operator action, intended recipient/destination/channel, device-reported time, result, and available external receipt. When the requested outcome includes delivery to the operator or another destination, Stage 30 workflow completion requires at least one successful authorized export or share attempt within the delivery record's scope. DELIVERY_STATE = AUTHORIZED permits the UI to say "Delivery authorized." It may say "Delivery attempted" only after the action receipt exists. It may say "Delivered" only when current evidence attributable to the recipient, destination, channel, or external system establishes transfer at its actual epistemic basis. The application cannot prevent or count transfers performed outside its controlled action path and must display that limitation. It does not claim it can undo a completed external transfer.

requirements.controllingText: An optional archive is only a transport representation of the same logical container. It must use the registered deterministic archive profile and pass the archive safety rules. The current profile is closed-loop-archive-profile/1: a ZIP archive containing only STORE (uncompressed) entries, entries ordered by canonical-path unsigned byte order, the UTF-8 filename flag set, every timestamp fixed to 1980-01-01T00:00:00, no directory entries, no symlinks or special entries, no archive comment, no encryption, and no extra fields except a Zip64 field exactly where an entry or archive size requires it. The manifest is always at `manifest.json`; the authoritative prompt is at `instruction.txt`; an inbound response is at `response.json`. Directory entries, timestamps, permissions, compression method, compression level, and path normalization are fixed by the registered archive profile. An archive mismatch does not alter the logical package identity; it rejects the transport representation.

atomicObligation.statement: For an application-produced optional archive, the deterministic application-produced archive contains no symlinks.

requirements.controllingText: Every artifact and package member is classified PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED, CREDENTIAL_SECRET, or UNKNOWN. CREDENTIAL_SECRET is never externally transferred. RESTRICTED or UNKNOWN content requires current recipient/provider suitability and human disclosure authorization. Package creation uses a derived allowlist, prohibited-member exclusion, known secret-pattern scan, path scan, disclosure check, and supported metadata inventory. A clean heuristic scan is not proof of absence. Redaction creates a new artifact and never silently replaces the original.

requirements.controllingText: The current registries are closed-loop-json-selector/1 and closed-loop-xml-selector/1. closed-loop-json-selector/1 MUST support at least: the root `$`; child access by identifier name and by single-quoted bracket name; nonnegative array index; and the wildcard `*` over object values and array elements. Selection order is document order. Recursive descent, filters, unions, slices, and script expressions are excluded from version 1. closed-loop-xml-selector/1 MUST support at least: absolute child-element paths from the document root; the element wildcard `*`; 1-based positional index predicates; attribute access `@name`; and `text()` value extraction. All other axes, predicates, and functions are excluded from version 1. A proposition that cannot be faithfully expressed within these registered subsets is not natively representable and routes externally.

requirements.controllingText: NFC normalization and default case folding use Unicode 15.1.0 data. Confusable detection uses the Unicode Technical Standard #39 confusables data published for Unicode 15.1.0. These exact data identities and table digests are recorded in the runtime registry and deployment manifest. A host Unicode implementation may be used only when startup and CI conformance fixtures establish the pinned results for every supported code-point class; otherwise the application uses bundled pinned tables. An unknown host/table mismatch blocks canonical filename normalization and package activation. Runtime upgrades do not silently change canonical identities; runtime or browser Unicode behavior may not silently redefine canonical identity. Every set-valued array has one named versioned normalizer. Every contentSha256, recordSha256, project hash, package hash, proof hash, scope hash, and terminal hash has a closed JSON-pointer inclusion and omission set registered in workflow-schema.js. No implementation selects preimage fields implicitly.

requirements.controllingText: closed-loop-encrypted-export/1 uses AES-256-GCM with a fresh 96-bit cryptographically random IV per encrypted payload, a fresh 128-bit random salt, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 with 600,000 iterations to derive the 256-bit key from the operator passphrase, and the canonical unencrypted package manifest digest as authenticated additional data. The container records algorithm, KDF, iterations, salt, IV, ciphertext length, and authentication tag. The passphrase and derived key are never persisted. IV reuse under one key is prohibited. Authentication failure rejects the export or restore without partial activation. CREDENTIAL_SECRET backup material requires this encrypted profile and cannot use an acknowledgment-only unencrypted export.

requirements.controllingText: Before the terminal Stage 30 calculation, the application creates a PRE_DELIVERY_CHECKPOINT bound to the exact Stage 27 through Stage 30 prerequisite records and every authorized artifact byte identity. The checkpoint is exported under the backup policy and its CHECKPOINT_ID is a terminal prerequisite and delivery-record field. The terminal prerequisite is satisfied only when the checkpoint custody state is at least BACKUP_EXPORT_ACTION_COMPLETED; BACKUP_PACKAGE_GENERATED alone is insufficient because an in-origin package is not an external backup. A later post-transfer checkpoint may be recorded but cannot retroactively satisfy preauthorization backup.

requirements.controllingText: A run execution attempt that ends REJECTED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED never counts toward the exactly-ten requirement and cannot satisfy any matrix cell. Its reservation reaches a terminal state, the same run target slot is re-reserved under Section 35.6, and the replacement attempt receives a new fresh context reserved for that run. The superseded context becomes historical, is excluded from the ten-distinct-context calculation, and its outputs cannot appear in any authorized input. Exactly the ten current accepted runs and their ten current distinct contexts satisfy Stage 11. An accepted run is never re-executed within the same iteration; a defect discovered in an accepted run routes through Stages 13-17.

requirements.controllingText: When clarification occurs outside the application, the final response may report the answer but cannot write a HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION field. An external agent may return the answer only as a proposed extracted human-origin value in humanAuthorityCandidates; the application MUST NOT classify that agent-reported value as HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION until the operator confirms or corrects it in the application. The application compares the reported answer with existing human records. A new human-origin value is presented for confirm or correct and recorded through a dedicated human command. Confirmation MUST be one-tap or direct edit of the proposed value; no retyping is required. Exact confirmation may use atomic co-acceptance under Section 14.10; a correction or inconsistency creates a new input version and replacement prompt. Confirmation does not apply to information already supplied.

If only a parsed representation is available, the application preserves the closed canonical representation together with original source digest, parser identity and version, source location, and the explicit reason original bytes were unavailable. Unknown extension data remains non-operational, non-gating, non-executable, excluded from prompts by default, and incapable of acquiring trust without an explicit schema migration.

requirements.controllingText: The application records a DELIVERY_ATTEMPT receipt containing the delivery ID, attempt ID, exact artifacts, byte hashes, operator action, intended recipient/destination/channel, device-reported time, result, and available external receipt. When the requested outcome includes delivery to the operator or another destination, Stage 30 workflow completion requires at least one successful authorized export or share attempt within the delivery record's scope. DELIVERY_STATE = AUTHORIZED permits the UI to say "Delivery authorized." It may say "Delivery attempted" only after the action receipt exists. It may say "Delivered" only when current evidence attributable to the recipient, destination, channel, or external system establishes transfer at its actual epistemic basis. The application cannot prevent or count transfers performed outside its controlled action path and must display that limitation. It does not claim it can undo a completed external transfer.

It lists canonical origin/base path, source commit, workflow run, build identity, canonicalization and registry identities, build command/environment, workflow-file digest, dependency/lockfile identities, CSP value, and every runtime HTML, JavaScript, CSS, worker, icon, manifest, schema, and asset path with media type, byte length, hash algorithm, and digest. The deployment manifest carries one overall manifest digest computed under closed-loop-canonical-json/1 with the digest field itself omitted; no manifest digest includes itself. Unmanifested runtime resources are prohibited.

requirements.controllingText: The application has no controlling service worker unless it is explicitly required, manifested, versioned, security-reviewed, and tested. Clean-profile and previously cached-profile acceptance must load one unmixed build identity or visibly block as stale. The running page, every script and style, and test-worker.js report or are bound to the expected build. Post-deployment verification retrieves every manifest path with cache bypass where supported and rejects missing, extra, redirected-to-different-content, cross-origin, stale, or modified resources. Browser acceptance proves the executed HTML, JavaScript, CSS, and worker resource graph matches the same manifest and build identity; mixed or stale cached builds fail.

Emit each line containing a character other than U+0009–U+000D or U+0020; if a nonempty string has no such line, emit that entire string as one unit. Empty strings, null and absent scalar values emit no content unit. Other scalar leaves emit one unit retaining their declared type and value. Original blank lines and exact original text remain available to the mandatory semantic reader even when the line projection emits no separate blank-line unit.

requirements.controllingText: For every supplied artifact occurrence, emit one inventory unit. Where exact bytes are valid UTF-8 and the text projection re-encodes to those exact bytes, also emit physical content units: scan left to right, treating CRLF as one terminator and otherwise CR, LF or form feed as a terminator; each unit contains the span through its terminator. Retain every nonempty span, including blank lines; emit a final unterminated span if present, but no zero-length trailing span. Coordinates start at page 1/line 1; form feed increments page and resets line to 1, other terminators increment line. BOM bytes, if present, remain part of the exact projection, not silently removed. This rule is accounting, not a claim that every UTF-8 artifact's media semantics have been parsed.

requirements.controllingText: For a mechanically supported structured-media subdivision, emit one structural unit per exposed page, section, archive member, embedded document/object, comment, annotation, tracked change or metadata object, using its exact parent and source locator; traverse children in source order, breaking any absent source-order tie by unsigned Unicode-scalar locator order. Recurse into textual leaves using the physical-content rule and into child media using this rule. A structural node is counted once per occurrence/location/kind; a node's structural unit and its descendant content units are distinct. Preserve inaccessible exposed nodes as INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED; do not fabricate children. Detailed coverage requires a closed format mapping that is part of this named versioned normative algorithm or an explicitly identified versioned normative format mapping authorized under §34.3. Merely publishing an implementation descriptor does not authorize such semantics. The mapping must fix node kinds, source locators, ordering, exact canonical source values and child extraction. This insertion adds no format-specific adapter or mapping. A claim of supported detailed coverage without that normative mapping is blocked; genuinely unsupported formats retain the fallback below. A mechanically available subdivision cannot be suppressed or relabeled unsupported to avoid that blocker.

Detailed coverage requires a closed format mapping that is part of this named versioned normative algorithm or an explicitly identified versioned normative format mapping authorized under §34.3. Merely publishing an implementation descriptor does not authorize such semantics. The mapping must fix node kinds, source locators, ordering, exact canonical source values and child extraction. requirements.controllingText: Apply the same recognition test to each supplied root and each verified expanded child. A byte candidate exists if the first four bytes are a ZIP local-header, EOCD, ZIP64 EOCD or ZIP64-locator signature (respectively hexadecimal 504b0304, 504b0506, 504b0606, 504b0607), or if the EOCD signature 504b0506 occurs anywhere in the last min(byteLength,65557) bytes. Also attempt validation when a supplied filename ends with .zip under ASCII case-insensitive comparison, or the supplied media type, before a semicolon and after ASCII whitespace trim/case-fold, is application/zip or application/x-zip-compressed. Names and media types can require an attempt but cannot suppress a byte candidate or establish success. A random signature or claimed filename can never create successful ZIP coverage: the complete retained structural, boundary, path and integrity checks decide that. Missing bytes retain an unavailable inventory/blocker; they do not establish absence of ZIP structure. Noncandidate bytes without a ZIP claim do not receive ZIP nodes through speculation; C's other available accounting rules remain applicable.

requirements.controllingText: Use a centralized, versioned intake profile closed-loop-raw-units-zip-limits/1. Its bounds are: 27 cumulative central-directory entries across the entire selected input-version archive-mapping pass, including every supplied root and recursively decoded child; 67108864 bytes per expanded member; 70254592 cumulative reserved-or-produced expanded bytes; 140509184 cumulative archive bytes submitted to decoding (count a nested archive again when it is submitted); compression ratio at most 1100 per member; filename byte length at most 65535; canonical path depth at most 128; maximum archive nesting level 27 with the supplied archive at level 1; and one cumulative elapsed-worker deadline of 600000 ms for that entire input-version archive-mapping pass. The entry budget is charged on exposure before expansion, including unsupported/blocked entries; the maximum depth cannot bypass that budget. requirements.controllingText: 5. One child ARTIFACT_INVENTORY with occurrence P followed by i and inventory locator [], binding the actual expanded byte length and H(expanded bytes) by C. Then emit that child's exact verified UTF-8 physical spans when C permits them, using offsets in the expanded child bytes, and apply the recursive rule below before proceeding to entry i+1. A recursively mapped child archive uses this already-emitted inventory and physical spans without emitting them a second time. The ZIP_MEMBER structural node and child inventory are different accounting obligations and both count. Metadata/comment nodes are not child files and do not receive inventory units. This mapping creates no semantic XML/JSON/CSV/Office/PDF section or annotation units from a member's contents; plain supported UTF-8 spans do not claim such parsing or inspection.

requirements.controllingText: For every verified expanded child, apply the byte/claim recognition test above. A ZIP candidate is mapped recursively by this same mapping, in depth-first central-directory order, under the entire input-version mapping pass's shared cumulative safety counters and deadline. The expanded child becomes the next archive occurrence P; no new root identity, fresh budget or favorable parent result is substituted. Exact expanded bytes remain retained and bound even when their own ZIP structure is blocked. A ZIP-based document can expose these ZIP members without thereby claiming semantic Office/XML/PDF parsing. A child that is not a ZIP candidate still receives its inventory and applicable exact UTF-8 physical spans under C; this addendum invents no other media mapping.

requirements.controllingText: When a depth, entry, byte, ratio, path, name, worker or work bound actually stops a recognized child, retain that child's already exposed member occurrence, inventory and available exact bytes, mark its unresolved subdivision INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED with the precise cause, and stop the affected expansion safely. It is neither a successful opaque fallback nor proof that children do not exist. Never reset counters for nested ZIPs, invoke unbounded recursive decompression, fabricate descendants, or treat unknown remaining units as zero. A separately supplied copy is a separate root occurrence with its own identity and is charged again to the same input-version pass counters; equality of bytes does not merge it or reset the budget.

requirements.controllingText: Every emitted inventory, member, metadata, comment and content unit participates in C's unchanged greater-than-500 raw-unit trigger. The supplied-file/archive-member count includes the supplied archive occurrence once and each enumerated child member occurrence once; metadata/comments do not add file occurrences. Storage/expansion safety budgets remain separate from these review triggers and retain their original enforcement.

requirements.controllingText: A supplied archive always retains its C inventory, exact original bytes when available, and a precise outcome. Distinguish (a) unsupported/encrypted structural features; (b) malformed/truncated/inconsistent structures, bad CRC or changed bytes; (c) unsafe/duplicate/colliding member identities; (d) absent/unreadable required bytes or unavailable decompressor/worker; and (e) resource-limit, timeout or interrupted execution. None is a successful parse or a favorable whole-file completeness result. Keep the exact typed cause and existing recovery route; do not silently drop the failing member, retry with weaker validation or invent child bytes.

requirements.controllingText: Only fully verified members receive ACCESSIBLE ZIP_MEMBER values with observed expanded hashes/lengths. An exposed member means a central-directory record with the exact central signature and complete in-bounds fixed header, filename, extra area and comment area, within the established central-directory extent and traversal order. Its entry index and central-header offset establish the member locator even when local validation or expansion fails. Preserve each such exposed occurrence, including duplicate names, directories, links and unsupported entries, as INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED with value=null when it cannot be validated; do not expand it or grant its path authority. It still receives exactly one child ARTIFACT_INVENTORY at P followed by i under C: when verified expanded bytes are unavailable, both byteLength and contentSha256 are null, with an explicit blocked disposition. A claimed member size or digest does not fill these values. Distinct colliding/duplicate central occurrences are never merged to hide them. No child inventory is created for a guessed entry, unparsed count or incomplete/unbounded central record.

requirements.controllingText: Preserve independently established exact metadata and comment spans as their corresponding ACCESSIBLE structural units even when the owning member is blocked; accessibility here concerns the exact metadata bytes, not the member's safe expansion or semantic validity. An extra field receives its specified unit only when its own 4-byte header and full declared payload are in bounds; duplicate/unsupported fields can be preserved as separate observed bytes but still block member admission. If malformed metadata prevents complete field segmentation, preserve the exact whole extra-area bytes as diagnostic provenance on the blocked occurrence, without inventing extra-field units. For a blocked member whose local metadata is not safely established, emit only established central metadata/extras/comments, then its blocked child inventory. This is bounded read-only exposure; it does not relax existing decoder rejection. Unknown remaining structure remains an explicit archive-level blocker, and a smaller observed count cannot discharge it.

requirements.controllingText: Preserve independently established exact metadata and comment spans as their corresponding ACCESSIBLE structural units even when the owning member is blocked; accessibility here concerns the exact metadata bytes, not the member's safe expansion or semantic validity. An extra field receives its specified unit only when its own 4-byte header and full declared payload are in bounds; duplicate/unsupported fields can be preserved as separate observed bytes but still block member admission. If malformed metadata prevents complete field segmentation, preserve the exact whole extra-area bytes as diagnostic provenance on the blocked occurrence, without inventing extra-field units. For a blocked member whose local metadata is not safely established, emit only established central metadata/extras/comments, then its blocked child inventory. This is bounded read-only exposure; it does not relax existing decoder rejection. Unknown remaining structure remains an explicit archive-level blocker, and a smaller observed count cannot discharge it.

requirements.controllingText: For SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, an absent/null/empty-string answer, or an empty MULTI_CHOICE array, is unanswered; a blocking request rejects it. A nonmissing TEXT or LONG_TEXT answer is a nonblank string; BOOLEAN is Boolean; NUMBER is either a JSON safe integer other than negative zero, or a string rational:N/D where N is a nonzero signed base-10 integer with no plus or leading zeros, D is a positive base-10 integer with no leading zeros, and gcd(abs(N),D)=1. D=1 is permitted only when N is outside the JSON safe-integer range. Zero is represented only by JSON integer 0. Other strings and typed objects are rejected; saving preserves this canonical representation; CHOICE is one exact allowed string; MULTI_CHOICE is an ordered duplicate-free array of exact allowed strings; DATE is a valid Gregorian calendar date in four-digit YYYY-MM-DD form with year 0001–9999, validated without time-zone conversion; FILE_REFERENCE is one current canonical artifact ID in the same project. Optional unanswered requests confer no factual assertion. Successful saving has precisely the existing §18 invalidation and replacement consequences.

A failed review uses the existing reconciliation/replacement/invalidation lifecycle. No user-operated reference creation is required. The expression's proposition must be availability of the exact target identified by the owning obligation's current scope; the appropriate agent proposes its semantic meaning and composition, and the application validates it.

requirements.controllingText: The expression uses only the existing LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF and AT_LEAST_K language, existing valid leaf targets, evidence classes, truth extraction, accepted sufficiency review and current-scope bindings. requirements.controllingText: COMPARE has optional operator with exact enum EQ, NE, GT, GTE, LT, LTE and default EQ. Its optional numericMode has exactly INTEGER, DECIMAL_STRING, APPROXIMATE; omission means the ordinary exact comparison described below, with no mode inferred from tolerance presence. ASSERT_EQ accepts the same optional numericMode and tolerances. No other assertion accepts numericMode or tolerances. Explicit INTEGER remains accepted and preserves ordinary exact comparison: canonical equality for nonnumeric canonical values, and safe-integer equality if either operand is a JSON number (then both must be safe integers). The name INTEGER does not coerce strings or prohibit ordinary nonnumeric canonical equality. Omitted mode follows the same rule. NE is the logical complement of EQ under the selected mode; invalid operands do not become a true NE.

requirements.controllingText: The exact typed DECIMAL representation is a closed object with exactly the two required non-null keys numberType and value: numberType is the string DECIMAL; value is a string matching -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)? whose mathematical value is not negative zero. Fractional trailing zeros are accepted; an empty fractional part, plus, whitespace, exponent, leading integer zeros, nulls, extra keys, and numeric value in place of the string are rejected. This same decimal-text grammar is used for canonical plain decimal strings in APPROXIMATE; it is deliberately stricter than DECIMAL_STRING mode. SORT's DECIMAL domain requires these typed objects, compares mathematical values exactly, and preserves each original object; it does not rewrite equivalent decimal spellings. Safe-integer numeric values belong to SORT INTEGER, not DECIMAL.

requirements.controllingText: APPROXIMATE applies only to COMPARE EQ/NE or ASSERT_EQ and requires an explicit absTol or relTol (or its compatibility alias). Operands and tolerances accept a JSON safe integer other than negative zero, a canonical plain decimal string as just defined, or that exact typed DECIMAL object. Operands may be negative; tolerances must be mathematically nonnegative. At least one tolerance component is explicit; the omitted component is zero. Use exact arithmetic: |actual-expected| <= max(absTol, relTol × max(|actual|,|expected|)). Approximate NE is the logical complement of that equality result. Compatibility names absoluteTolerance and relativeTolerance map to absTol and relTol; when both names for a component appear they must normalize to exactly the same mathematical value, otherwise reject the definition. Unsupported precision is UNDETERMINED. These aliases authorize no other default.

Operands may be negative; tolerances must be mathematically nonnegative. At least one tolerance component is explicit; the omitted component is zero. Compatibility names absoluteTolerance and relativeTolerance map to absTol and relTol; when both names for a component appear they must normalize to exactly the same mathematical value, otherwise reject the definition. Unsupported precision is UNDETERMINED. These aliases authorize no other default.

requirements.controllingText: JSON selector syntax is $ followed by zero or more .identifier, .*, [index], [*], or ['name'] segments. Identifier is [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*; index is 0 or a nonzero digit followed by digits and must be safe; bracket names allow only escaped single quote or escaped backslash. Child access addresses object members, index access addresses arrays, and wildcard addresses object values or array elements. Without wildcard return the selected value; with wildcard return an ordered array of matches. Parsed JSON retains source member order and CSV objects retain header order; objects without source order use §34.1 key order. Array order is retained. Missing branches contribute no match; if a segment has no matches, the result is UNDETERMINED. Selecting a present empty array without a wildcard returns that empty array.

requirements.controllingText: XML selectors start with exactly one slash, then child-element segments named [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]* or *, optionally followed by [positive safe integer]. The first segment matches the document element at position 1; later positions apply within each parent's matching child elements. Only the final segment may be @name or text(). Element results are arrays of the canonical element-node values defined in D4; attribute results are arrays of existing exact attribute strings; text() returns one string per selected element, concatenating descendant text/CDATA in document order and excluding comments. A wholly empty selection at any segment, including a final attribute selection, is UNDETERMINED. A selected element with no text yields the known empty string, not a missing selection. Other selector syntax is invalid before execution.

requirements.controllingText: PARSE_XML returns the document element as a canonical JSON object with exactly four required non-null properties: name (exact element-name string), attributes (object of exact parsed attribute-name/string-value pairs), children (ordered array of its immediate element-node values), and content (ordered array of strings and immediate element-node values in source content order). Every child appears once in children and once as the same canonical value in content; this is duplicated value content, not a cyclic pointer or identity-based equality. Each nonempty ordinary text run between markup boundaries contributes one decoded string; each nonempty CDATA body contributes one literal string. Empty runs are omitted, comments contribute no entry, adjacent strings separated by comment/CDATA boundaries are not coalesced, and entity references within a text run are decoded into that one string. Outside-root whitespace and the declaration are not represented. Attribute order has no canonical-equality significance; child/content array order and text-run segmentation do. Thus differently ordered attributes with equal values compare equal, while mixed text/child content remains observable in exact document order. XML name/attribute/character normalization is precisely the parsing rule above, not namespace inference.

requirements.controllingText: These canonical node values may be consumed by canonical equality, UNIQUE, ASSERT_SET_EQUAL and SELECT_JSON_PATH without opaque host-object behavior. For JSON-path traversal their object keys, including attributes, use §34.1 key order; XML traversal uses children/content source order. SELECT_XML requires a parsed node value from PARSE_XML or a node selected from that parsed value in the same execution; a lookalike authored JSON object does not acquire XML-node provenance. Provenance does not affect canonical equality. Its input is one node, not an implicitly unwrapped array; extraction from an element-result array is explicit through SELECT_JSON_PATH.

requirements.controllingText: Regex retains §21.9's required JavaScript-compatible subset. Flags are an optional string of unique i, m, s, u characters, default empty. Matching uses those flags with fresh match state; no global/sticky state is accepted. In addition to §21.9's listed constructs, allow word-boundary \b/\B and literal escapes \f, \n, \r, \t, \v, \xHH, \uHHHH and escaped punctuation under the selected flags. requirements.controllingText: For the conditional native route of 07 EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST, 15 EXECUTE_REGRESSION, 19 REGRESSION_VERIFY, and the 38 F1 pairs, the input-binding minimum is APPLICATION_OBSERVED. The application establishes that basis from actual custody and verification of each required exact input, its current identity/hash and scope, before execution may start. This is not a requirement that execution has already succeeded: execution outcome, isolation, provenance, disposition and evidence sufficiency are separately determined from the actual execution. An absent or mismatched required input blocks native execution; a download, actor echo or route label does not satisfy this native minimum. This clause does not change the execution mode or permit an unapproved fallback to a different executor. Existing application, human-decision and operator commands outside these conditional pairs retain their existing source contracts; no external evidence minimum is assigned to them by this amendment.

requirements.controllingText: Accepted authoring forms are (1) records.tests[i].fields.EXPECTED_VARIANCE_CONTRACT, an embedded object with those lower-camel-case names, and (2) records.expectedVarianceContracts[i].fields.DIMENSIONS, .ALLOWED_VARIANCE and optional .RATIONALE, with TEST_ID in that record's relationships member. The latter is exactly relationships.TEST_ID = {"tempKey":"<same-response tests tempKey>"} or {"recordId":"<operation-supplied current tests ID>"}, resolved through the existing ingestion path. No direct authored application-owned TEST_ID field is accepted. Map only those three direct names to their lower-camel-case counterparts. Embedded additional canonical-JSON properties are preserved exactly and included in the semantic hash as nonoperative context; they cannot introduce executable meaning, a gate, evidence basis or favorable outcome. Direct records remain subject to their closed family registry; no arbitrary new direct field is permitted. If both forms address a test, their normalized objects must be canonical-byte-identical; disagreement or ambiguous duplicates block rather than choosing a winner. Byte-identical embedded and direct forms for the same resolved test produce exactly one current enclosing contract retaining provenance from both sources, never competing canonical contracts. Section 35.10 continues to require preservation of original extension bytes where available and default prompt exclusion. Hashing retained context establishes identity and invalidation only, never permission to execute it or to count it as favorable evidence.

requirements.controllingText: Use a centralized, versioned intake profile closed-loop-raw-units-zip-limits/1. Its bounds are: 27 cumulative central-directory entries across the entire selected input-version archive-mapping pass, including every supplied root and recursively decoded child; 67108864 bytes per expanded member; 70254592 cumulative reserved-or-produced expanded bytes; 140509184 cumulative archive bytes submitted to decoding (count a nested archive again when it is submitted); compression ratio at most 1100 per member; filename byte length at most 65535; canonical path depth at most 128; maximum archive nesting level 27 with the supplied archive at level 1; and one cumulative elapsed-worker deadline of 600000 ms for that entire input-version archive-mapping pass. The entry budget is charged on exposure before expansion, including unsupported/blocked entries; the maximum depth cannot bypass that budget. Expansion and byte accounting are checked before allocation and incrementally, against both declared and actual lengths; declared metadata never substitutes for verified bytes. The expansion safety counter reserves each declared output length before allocation; actual production within that reservation does not charge the same byte twice, while any additional produced byte must first fit and consume remaining budget. Every produced/reserved byte remains charged even if later CRC, validation or decoding fails; no refund, reset or retry can escape the pass-wide ceiling. It includes every child occurrence at every depth, including a nested archive's bytes as its parent's output and its own children separately. This work-safety counter is distinct from the semantic aggregate-byte review sum, which includes only actually verified retained child bytes. The archive-byte sum counts each archive occurrence once when submitted to decoding. The same original per-archive structural and byte checks remain; a bound can stop processing earlier, never authorize weaker checking. These ceilings reuse the current default decoder's 27 entries, 64 MiB file bound, 64 MiB + 1 MiB response + 2 MiB manifest total, twice-total archive bound, ratio/name/path/work bounds; the intake profile assigns those generic ceilings without granting any response.json/manifest.json role or larger filename-specific allowance. Transport recursiveExpansion=false and maxNestingDepth=0 remain response-transport rules, not intake accounting rules. A lower already-applicable storage/worker bound still stops work and remains explicitly blocked; it must not silently change this profile or yield favorable completeness. The exact profile-hash preimage is C({"version":"closed-loop-raw-units-zip-limits/1","scope":"INPUT_VERSION_PASS","maxEntries":27,"maxEntryBytes":67108864,"maxExpandedBytes":70254592,"maxArchiveBytes":140509184,"maxCompressionRatio":1100,"maxFilenameBytes":65535,"maxPathDepth":128,"maxNestingDepth":27,"workerTimeoutMs":600000}); its SHA-256 is the profile hash. The retained unitization derivation binds the owning input version, mapping ID, this exact profile ID/hash, actual counters and completion/blocker status; changed profile or source invalidates reuse under the existing derivation rules. Repeated equal roots and members are charged separately. Any future profile change follows existing versioning and acceptance requirements.

governors.controllingText:
The unit universe is structural accounting. Retain the exact originating input and artifact bytes; no normalized projection replaces them or asserts inspection. Each unit binds the input version, supplied occurrence, exact structural location and source-value hash. Enumerate roots in their retained source occurrence order; within a structured value visit arrays in index order and object keys in unsigned Unicode-scalar order. A canonical mirror of the same originating field is visited only once, using the originating field; separately supplied equal values are separate occurrences.

For human text and string-valued structured human input, CRLF, CR and LF delimit physical lines. Retain original line positions. Emit each line containing a character other than U+0009–U+000D or U+0020; if a nonempty string has no such line, emit that entire string as one unit. Empty strings, null and absent scalar values emit no content unit. Other scalar leaves emit one unit retaining their declared type and value. Original blank lines and exact original text remain available to the mandatory semantic reader even when the line projection emits no separate blank-line unit.

For every supplied artifact occurrence, emit one inventory unit. Where exact bytes are valid UTF-8 and the text projection re-encodes to those exact bytes, also emit physical content units: scan left to right, treating CRLF as one terminator and otherwise CR, LF or form feed as a terminator; each unit contains the span through its terminator. Retain every nonempty span, including blank lines; emit a final unterminated span if present, but no zero-length trailing span. Coordinates start at page 1/line 1; form feed increments page and resets line to 1, other terminators increment line. BOM bytes, if present, remain part of the exact projection, not silently removed. This rule is accounting, not a claim that every UTF-8 artifact's media semantics have been parsed.

For a mechanically supported structured-media subdivision, emit one structural unit per exposed page, section, archive member, embedded document/object, comment, annotation, tracked change or metadata object, using its exact parent and source locator; traverse children in source order, breaking any absent source-order tie by unsigned Unicode-scalar locator order. Recurse into textual leaves using the physical-content rule and into child media using this rule. A structural node is counted once per occurrence/location/kind; a node's structural unit and its descendant content units are distinct. Preserve inaccessible exposed nodes as INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED; do not fabricate children. Detailed coverage requires a closed format mapping that is part of this named versioned normative algorithm or an explicitly identified versioned normative format mapping authorized under §34.3. Merely publishing an implementation descriptor does not authorize such semantics. The mapping must fix node kinds, source locators, ordering, exact canonical source values and child extraction. This insertion adds no format-specific adapter or mapping. A claim of supported detailed coverage without that normative mapping is blocked; genuinely unsupported formats retain the fallback below. A mechanically available subdivision cannot be suppressed or relabeled unsupported to avoid that blocker.

Subdivision is additive: an exact UTF-8 whole-file projection emits its physical spans even when a supported structured mapping also emits structural nodes and textual leaves. Whole-file spans, structural nodes and structural textual-leaf spans have distinct kinds and locators and are all counted; overlap in underlying bytes does not deduplicate these different accounting obligations. Each archive-member or embedded-file occurrence emits both its parent structural occurrence unit and its own child inventory unit, followed by its own supported content/subdivisions. A textual leaf is not a child file and gets no inventory unit. Repeated references to the same emitted unit still deduplicate under the rule below.

Source hashes and binding are closed as follows. C(x) means the exact UTF-8 bytes of §34.1 canonical JSON; H(b) means lowercase SHA-256 hexadecimal of exact bytes b. Source-value hash preimages by kind are:
- HUMAN_TEXT_LINE or HUMAN_TEXT_WHOLE: C({"type":"STRING","value":s}), where s is the exact emitted line excluding its terminator, or the entire whitespace-only nonempty string respectively. Physical line number and original field pointer retain position; retained originating bytes preserve terminators.
- HUMAN_SCALAR: C({"type":t,"value":v}), where t is the declared scalar type and v its exact canonical value; no string coercion. Null/absent values remain excluded as above.
- ARTIFACT_INVENTORY: C({"byteLength":n,"contentSha256":h}), where n is exact byte length and h=H(exact artifact bytes). If bytes are unavailable, both values are null; asserted length/digest remains source context, never substituted for observed bytes. The unit remains inaccessible/blocked, with its retained occurrence/locator binding.
- PHYSICAL_SPAN: the exact original byte span including its terminator, without canonical JSON wrapping. Its locator binds zero-based byte start and exclusive end plus the one-based page/line coordinates.
- STRUCTURAL_NODE: C({"nodeKind":k,"status":q,"value":v}), where k and v are the exact kind and canonical source value fixed by the authorized format mapping, and q is ACCESSIBLE or INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED. Inaccessible nodes have v=null; exact exposed parent/locator and k remain bound. No invented serialization of an adapter object is permitted.
- STRUCTURAL_TEXT_SPAN: exact UTF-8 bytes of the mapped exact textual leaf's physical span, including its terminator. The authorized mapping identifies the leaf and its exact extraction; no silent whitespace normalization is allowed.

Each unit's binding hash preimage is C({"algorithm":"closed-loop-raw-units/1","inputVersion":V,"occurrence":O,"kind":K,"locator":L,"sourceValueSha256":S}). V is the exact owning input-version identity string; O is the ordered zero-based safe-integer path of supplied root and, where applicable, child-member occurrence indices; K is exactly one of the seven uppercase kinds above; S is the corresponding source-value hash. L is an ordered locator array: human units use [originating JSON pointer, one-based physical line] or [originating JSON pointer] for whole strings/scalars; inventories use []; whole-file spans use [startByte,endByte,page,line]; structural nodes use [normative format mapping ID, exact mapping locator]; structural textual spans append [startByte,endByte,page,line] to their structural-leaf locator. Byte offsets for a structural textual leaf refer to its exact UTF-8 extraction. The source-value hash alone does not identify the occurrence: binding hash plus retained input/source supplies the exact type, location and occurrence. These accounting hashes/locators are not §34.2 canonical record IDs. Distinct roots are numbered in retained source occurrence order, including separately supplied identical roots; a canonical mirror does not receive a second root number.

An image/media occurrence without a supported finer subdivision uses its inventory unit as its whole-media unit. A format with no supported mechanically available subdivision likewise uses its inventory unit as the whole-file fallback, with an explicit unsupported/unavailable-subdivision basis and the original bytes retained. These fallbacks neither prove inspection nor remove existing material uncertainty/blockers. Comments, annotations, tracked changes, metadata and embedded content are not discarded as nonsemantic.

Deduplicate only repeated accounting references to the same occurrence, kind, location and exact source-value hash. Never merge distinct supplied occurrences, even with identical hashes. Order and retained source identity determine stable accounting references; canonical record IDs still use §34.2. Count the entire resulting unit universe, including inventory, structural and inaccessible units, when applying the unchanged §6.5A limits. The raw-unit challenge condition is strictly greater than 500, not greater than or equal to 500; every other size-independent trigger remains effective.

Every emitted inventory, member, metadata, comment and content unit participates in C's unchanged greater-than-500 raw-unit trigger. The supplied-file/archive-member count includes the supplied archive occurrence once and each enumerated child member occurrence once; metadata/comments do not add file occurrences. For the existing aggregate-supplied-byte challenge, count each retained file occurrence's actual bytes once: the original compressed archive plus each verified expanded child occurrence at every recursive depth; do not count metadata byte spans again or deduplicate equal occurrences. Apply the existing per-text/document and mechanically countable-page thresholds to eligible original/child content by their existing rules. This additive count can trigger review sooner than treating an archive as one opaque file; no threshold value is raised or reduced. Storage/expansion safety budgets remain separate from these review triggers and retain their original enforcement.

Failure and unknown content
A supplied archive always retains its C inventory, exact original bytes when available, and a precise outcome. Distinguish (a) unsupported/encrypted structural features; (b) malformed/truncated/inconsistent structures, bad CRC or changed bytes; (c) unsafe/duplicate/colliding member identities; (d) absent/unreadable required bytes or unavailable decompressor/worker; and (e) resource-limit, timeout or interrupted execution. None is a successful parse or a favorable whole-file completeness result. Keep the exact typed cause and existing recovery route; do not silently drop the failing member, retry with weaker validation or invent child bytes.

Only fully verified members receive ACCESSIBLE ZIP_MEMBER values with observed expanded hashes/lengths. An exposed member means a central-directory record with the exact central signature and complete in-bounds fixed header, filename, extra area and comment area, within the established central-directory extent and traversal order. Its entry index and central-header offset establish the member locator even when local validation or expansion fails. Preserve each such exposed occurrence, including duplicate names, directories, links and unsupported entries, as INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED with value=null when it cannot be validated; do not expand it or grant its path authority. It still receives exactly one child ARTIFACT_INVENTORY at P followed by i under C: when verified expanded bytes are unavailable, both byteLength and contentSha256 are null, with an explicit blocked disposition. A claimed member size or digest does not fill these values. Distinct colliding/duplicate central occurrences are never merged to hide them. No child inventory is created for a guessed entry, unparsed count or incomplete/unbounded central record.

Preserve independently established exact metadata and comment spans as their corresponding ACCESSIBLE structural units even when the owning member is blocked; accessibility here concerns the exact metadata bytes, not the member's safe expansion or semantic validity. An extra field receives its specified unit only when its own 4-byte header and full declared payload are in bounds; duplicate/unsupported fields can be preserved as separate observed bytes but still block member admission. If malformed metadata prevents complete field segmentation, preserve the exact whole extra-area bytes as diagnostic provenance on the blocked occurrence, without inventing extra-field units. For a blocked member whose local metadata is not safely established, emit only established central metadata/extras/comments, then its blocked child inventory. This is bounded read-only exposure; it does not relax existing decoder rejection. Unknown remaining structure remains an explicit archive-level blocker, and a smaller observed count cannot discharge it.

Also attempt validation when a supplied filename ends with .zip under ASCII case-insensitive comparison, or the supplied media type, before a semicolon and after ASCII whitespace trim/case-fold, is application/zip or application/x-zip-compressed. Names and media types can require an attempt but cannot suppress a byte candidate or establish success. A random signature or claimed filename can never create successful ZIP coverage: the complete retained structural, boundary, path and integrity checks decide that. Missing bytes retain an unavailable inventory/blocker; they do not establish absence of ZIP structure. Noncandidate bytes without a ZIP claim do not receive ZIP nodes through speculation; C's other available accounting rules remain applicable.

Use a centralized, versioned intake profile closed-loop-raw-units-zip-limits/1. Its bounds are: 27 cumulative central-directory entries across the entire selected input-version archive-mapping pass, including every supplied root and recursively decoded child; 67108864 bytes per expanded member; 70254592 cumulative reserved-or-produced expanded bytes; 140509184 cumulative archive bytes submitted to decoding (count a nested archive again when it is submitted); compression ratio at most 1100 per member; filename byte length at most 65535; canonical path depth at most 128; maximum archive nesting level 27 with the supplied archive at level 1; and one cumulative elapsed-worker deadline of 600000 ms for that entire input-version archive-mapping pass. The entry budget is charged on exposure before expansion, including unsupported/blocked entries; the maximum depth cannot bypass that budget. Expansion and byte accounting are checked before allocation and incrementally, against both declared and actual lengths; declared metadata never substitutes for verified bytes. The expansion safety counter reserves each declared output length before allocation; actual production within that reservation does not charge the same byte twice, while any additional produced byte must first fit and consume remaining budget. Every produced/reserved byte remains charged even if later CRC, validation or decoding fails; no refund, reset or retry can escape the pass-wide ceiling. It includes every child occurrence at every depth, including a nested archive's bytes as its parent's output and its own children separately. This work-safety counter is distinct from the semantic aggregate-byte review sum, which includes only actually verified retained child bytes. These ceilings reuse the current default decoder's 27 entries, 64 MiB file bound, 64 MiB + 1 MiB response + 2 MiB manifest total, twice-total archive bound, ratio/name/path/work bounds; the intake profile assigns those generic ceilings without granting any response.json/manifest.json role or larger filename-specific allowance. Every ZIP structural unit's locator is ["closed-loop-raw-units-zip/1", locatorValue], where locatorValue is one of the exact ordered arrays below. All offsets and lengths are nonnegative safe integers measured in the parent archive's original bytes; an index is a zero-based safe integer. A node with verified source bytes has status ACCESSIBLE. An empty comment creates no comment unit. No character-set guess or interpretation makes comment bytes executable or favorable evidence.

Then, for every entry i in central-directory order, emit in this exact order:
1. One ZIP_MEMBER structural node, with occurrence P and locatorValue ["MEMBER", i, centralHeaderOffset]. No timestamp, name or claimed digest substitutes for observed member bytes.

ZIP_MEMBER_METADATA nodes for the central fixed header, local fixed header and data descriptor if present, in that order. locatorValue is ["MEMBER_METADATA", i, recordType, offset], with recordType CENTRAL_HEADER, LOCAL_HEADER or DATA_DESCRIPTOR. v has exactly recordType, offset, byteLength and rawHex. Filename, extras and comment bytes are excluded from these fixed-header units because their exact representations are bound separately.

One ZIP_EXTRA_FIELD node per actually present local extra field, followed by one per actually present central extra field; preserve byte order within each area, including separately present equal fields in the two areas. locatorValue is ["EXTRA_FIELD", i, area, ordinal, offset], with area LOCAL or CENTRAL and ordinal zero-based within that area. v has exactly area, headerId, offset, byteLength and rawHex. byteLength and rawHex cover the full 4-byte ID/length header plus its declared payload. 5. One child ARTIFACT_INVENTORY with occurrence P followed by i and inventory locator [], binding the actual expanded byte length and H(expanded bytes) by C. Then emit that child's exact verified UTF-8 physical spans when C permits them, using offsets in the expanded child bytes, and apply the recursive rule below before proceeding to entry i+1. A recursively mapped child archive uses this already-emitted inventory and physical spans without emitting them a second time. The ZIP_MEMBER structural node and child inventory are different accounting obligations and both count. Metadata/comment nodes are not child files and do not receive inventory units. This mapping creates no semantic XML/JSON/CSV/Office/PDF section or annotation units from a member's contents; plain supported UTF-8 spans do not claim such parsing or inspection.

Recursive child media
For every verified expanded child, apply the byte/claim recognition test above. A ZIP candidate is mapped recursively by this same mapping, in depth-first central-directory order, under the entire input-version mapping pass's shared cumulative safety counters and deadline. The expanded child becomes the next archive occurrence P; no new root identity, fresh budget or favorable parent result is substituted. Exact expanded bytes remain retained and bound even when their own ZIP structure is blocked. A ZIP-based document can expose these ZIP members without thereby claiming semantic Office/XML/PDF parsing. A child that is not a ZIP candidate still receives its inventory and applicable exact UTF-8 physical spans under C; this addendum invents no other media mapping.

When a depth, entry, byte, ratio, path, name, worker or work bound actually stops a recognized child, retain that child's already exposed member occurrence, inventory and available exact bytes, mark its unresolved subdivision INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED with the precise cause, and stop the affected expansion safely. It is neither a successful opaque fallback nor proof that children do not exist. Never reset counters for nested ZIPs, invoke unbounded recursive decompression, fabricate descendants, or treat unknown remaining units as zero. A separately supplied copy is a separate root occurrence with its own identity and is charged again to the same input-version pass counters; equality of bytes does not merge it or reset the budget.

Counting and thresholds
Every emitted inventory, member, metadata, comment and content unit participates in C's unchanged greater-than-500 raw-unit trigger. The supplied-file/archive-member count includes the supplied archive occurrence once and each enumerated child member occurrence once; metadata/comments do not add file occurrences. For the existing aggregate-supplied-byte challenge, count each retained file occurrence's actual bytes once: the original compressed archive plus each verified expanded child occurrence at every recursive depth; do not count metadata byte spans again or deduplicate equal occurrences. Apply the existing per-text/document and mechanically countable-page thresholds to eligible original/child content by their existing rules. This additive count can trigger review sooner than treating an archive as one opaque file; no threshold value is raised or reduced. Storage/expansion safety budgets remain separate from these review triggers and retain their original enforcement.

Failure and unknown content
A supplied archive always retains its C inventory, exact original bytes when available, and a precise outcome. Distinguish (a) unsupported/encrypted structural features; (b) malformed/truncated/inconsistent structures, bad CRC or changed bytes; (c) unsafe/duplicate/colliding member identities; (d) absent/unreadable required bytes or unavailable decompressor/worker; and (e) resource-limit, timeout or interrupted execution. None is a successful parse or a favorable whole-file completeness result. Keep the exact typed cause and existing recovery route; do not silently drop the failing member, retry with weaker validation or invent child bytes.

Only fully verified members receive ACCESSIBLE ZIP_MEMBER values with observed expanded hashes/lengths. An exposed member means a central-directory record with the exact central signature and complete in-bounds fixed header, filename, extra area and comment area, within the established central-directory extent and traversal order. Its entry index and central-header offset establish the member locator even when local validation or expansion fails. Preserve each such exposed occurrence, including duplicate names, directories, links and unsupported entries, as INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED with value=null when it cannot be validated; do not expand it or grant its path authority. It still receives exactly one child ARTIFACT_INVENTORY at P followed by i under C: when verified expanded bytes are unavailable, both byteLength and contentSha256 are null, with an explicit blocked disposition. A claimed member size or digest does not fill these values. Distinct colliding/duplicate central occurrences are never merged to hide them. Preserve independently established exact metadata and comment spans as their corresponding ACCESSIBLE structural units even when the owning member is blocked; accessibility here concerns the exact metadata bytes, not the member's safe expansion or semantic validity. An extra field receives its specified unit only when its own 4-byte header and full declared payload are in bounds; duplicate/unsupported fields can be preserved as separate observed bytes but still block member admission. If malformed metadata prevents complete field segmentation, preserve the exact whole extra-area bytes as diagnostic provenance on the blocked occurrence, without inventing extra-field units. Unknown remaining structure remains an explicit archive-level blocker, and a smaller observed count cannot discharge it.

A structurally established zero-entry EOCD with zero central-directory size and consistent offsets is a known empty archive, not malformed merely because the existing decoder rejects count=0. Preserve its inventory and exposed control/comment nodes, emit no invented member or child inventory, and record EMPTY_ARCHIVE_DECODER_BOUNDARY as INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED for detailed decoding under this current parser scope. It does not yield a successful detailed-coverage claim or unsupported-format fallback. A missing or unusable DEFLATE implementation/worker is unavailable evidence, not unsupported ZIP format; preserve originals, established nodes and blocked child inventories. Corrupt bytes, an unsupported feature, unsafe paths, actual resource exhaustion and unavailable machinery retain distinct causes and recovery requirements.

This mapping adopts accounting order, unit granularity, raw-name/metadata/comment identity, additive counts, recursive traversal and its explicit bounded intake profile only. It does not adopt arbitrary parser output as normative truth, authorize an unbounded parser or relaxed safety policy, establish semantic inspection, waive current evidence requirements, or accept historical coverage proof. Implementation must expose the required exact locators/bytes from the existing decoder without changing its retained safety predicates; actual boundary and fault tests remain due.
